card: Parallelizes compact block filter checking during wallet fast rescans, introducing a `-walletpar` configuration option to distribute filter evaluations across worker threads. Currently, BIP 157/158 fast rescans evaluate filters sequentially on one thread, making wallet recovery over large block intervals take several minutes despite minimal transaction matches. Mainnet benchmarks scanning 200,000 blocks show runtimes drop from 272s on master down to 34.8s using 8 threads (~7.8x speedup).
evidence: Author's hyperfine benchmarks scanning 200,000 blocks on mainnet (Intel Core Ultra 7 265) show rescan time dropping from 272.2s on master to 34.8s with `-walletpar=8`, an approximately 7.8x speedup (PR description)
Custom regtest benchmarks measuring worst-case payment intervals confirm parallel fast rescan outperforms serial fast rescan across sparse and dense descriptor matches (PR description)
problem: Wallet fast rescan with compact block filters (BIP 157/158) processes blocks sequentially on a single thread. Users rescanning large chain ranges or importing descriptors experience long wait times—taking minutes even when few or no transactions match—because multi-core hardware remains largely idle during filter evaluation.
scope_notes: Diff was not included in the prompt. Introduces threading concurrency and pipeline queue management into wallet rescan logic, with a new user-facing configuration parameter `-walletpar`.
summary: Parallelizes compact block filter checking during wallet fast rescans using a bounded worker thread pool. Adds a `-walletpar` startup option to configure worker threads up to a default maximum of 8, while preserving serialized transaction processing and wallet state updates on the main thread. When a keypool top-up occurs after matching a block, the checker patches in-flight non-matching block verdicts by testing only the newly derived descriptor scripts in parallel.
